format: lightsuffer-ios slice5 spatial effects fixture v1

notes.float_format: all floating point values are rounded to 7 significant digits
notes.spatial_effects: the deterministic spatial effects of the upstream engine: the highlight boost, the in emulsion scatter, the back reflection halation, the spatial diffusion of the DIR coupler inhibitors, the diffusion filters of the camera and of the enlarger, the lens blurs of the camera and of the scanner and the unsharp mask of the scanner.
notes.deferred: the grain and the glare are NOT part of this fixture: the grain needs the SciPy binomial and Poisson random variates and the glare needs a seeded lognormal, both of which are deferred to a later slice.
notes.film_format: the micrometre scale effects (the scatter, the halation and the inhibitor diffusion) need a pixel of a meaningful size: on a 32 x 32 image a 35 mm frame gives a pixel of 1093.75 um and the effects are below one pixel. The cases that exercise them use a 1 mm film format (31.25 um per pixel) and, for the scatter, the spatial scale knob of the upstream.

test_image.description: row 0: a neutral grey ramp log spaced 0.002..4.0; row 1: saturated colour patches; row 2: skin like colour patches; row 3: mixed patches (black, white, 50 % grey, 18 % grey, ...); rows 4-11: a dark field with a neutral highlight spot and a warm highlight spot; rows 12-31: a smooth vertical ramp on the left half and a textured field (numpy default_rng(20261110)) on the right half, separated by a hard vertical edge

notes.gaussians: fast_gaussian_filter(plane, sigma) of the upstream: the separable FIR below three pixels and the Young & van Vliet recursion above, both with the reflect boundary.
notes.exponentials: fast_exponential_filter(plane, decay) of the upstream: the Gaussian mixture surrogate of the isotropic 2D exponential PSF.
notes.reflect: the _reflect helper of the upstream for an axis of 7 samples

cases.title: Every spatial effect switched off
cases.description: The reference of the single effect cases: the scatter and the halation off, the DIR couplers active but per pixel (no inhibitor diffusion), the camera and the enlarger diffusion filters off, the lens blurs off and the unsharp mask off.

cases.title: The upstream defaults, with the grain off
cases.description: The upstream defaults of init_params(): the scatter and the halation active (with the stock preset of Portra 400), the DIR couplers active with their default 20 um inhibitor diffusion, the unsharp mask of the scanner at its default (0.7, 0.7). The grain and the glare are switched off (they are stochastic) and so is the auto exposure (not ported). On a 35 mm frame of a 32 x 32 image a pixel is 1093.75 um, so the micrometre scale effects are below one pixel.

cases.title: The scatter and the back reflection halation
cases.description: The scatter (a Gaussian core and an exponential tail) and the back reflection halation (three Gaussians with sqrt(k) spaced widths) of the negative, with the upstream parameters on a 1 mm film format (a pixel is 31.25 um) and with the spatial scale of the scatter multiplied by 20 so that both kernels cover several pixels.

cases.title: The highlight boost
cases.description: The boost that reconstructs the pre clip irradiance of the negative (boost_ev = 6, the upstream default range of 0.3 and the upstream default protection of 4 stops). The upstream default of boost_ev is 0, i.e. the boost is inactive.

cases.title: The spatial diffusion of the DIR coupler inhibitors
cases.description: The inhibitors released by the emulsion layers diffuse into the neighbourhood (a Gaussian of 20 um and an exponential tail of 200 um with a weight of 0.06, the upstream defaults) before they reduce the development of the neighbouring pixels. The case uses a 1 mm film format so that the diffusion covers several pixels.

cases.title: The diffusion filter of the camera
cases.description: The black pro mist family (the upstream default family) at a strength of 1.0 and a spatial scale of 8. The filter redistributes the light between the unscattered and the scattered population, with a per channel point spread function.

cases.title: The diffusion filter of the enlarger
cases.description: The same filter as the camera case, but applied on the exposure of the paper.

cases.title: The lens blur of the camera
cases.description: The 60 um lens blur of the camera, on a 1 mm film format (a pixel is 31.25 um, so the blur is 1.92 pixels wide).

cases.title: The lens blur and the unsharp mask of the scanner
cases.description: The lens blur of the scanner (1.5 pixels) and its unsharp mask (the upstream default of 0.7 pixels and 0.7 of amount), applied on the linear RGB of the scan, after the output gamut compression and before the output transfer function.

cases.title: Every deterministic spatial effect at once
cases.description: The scatter, the halation, the highlight boost, the DIR coupler diffusion, the camera and the enlarger diffusion filters, the lens blur of the camera and the lens blur and the unsharp mask of the scanner, all at once.
